data.description:
## The defect

`rebar/host` metrics published from the FIRST ~200 lines of `infra/scripts/observability.sh` —
`gerrit_healthy`, `reviewbot_healthy`, `GerritReachable`, `mcp_healthy`, `disk_used_percent`,
`root_disk_used_percent`, `gate_scratch_mounted` — show a max gap of **25 minutes**, widening
from 10 minutes in an earlier sweep the same day. At 20:47Z on 2026-09-05 that produced **four
simultaneous false alarms** (root-disk-pressure, gerrit-data-disk-high, gerrit-gate-down,
mcp-serving-path-down), every StateReason naming "missing datapoints were treated as
Breaching", while the underlying conditions were verified healthy: Gerrit HTTP 200 in 0.27 s,
root disk 71-76% against an 85% threshold, `disk_used_percent` = 20.

## Why this is NOT bug 9313 (ignitable-fuchsia-kawala)

`9313` is the section-truncation defect: the probe is SIGTERM-ed on its 240s `TimeoutStartSec`
inside the docker `du`, so every metric published AFTER that point vanishes. It is proven in
situ, and change 2684 fixes it.

**It cannot produce a head gap.** The head runs BEFORE the docker walk. The breadcrumb trace
taken for `9313` covers ten consecutive killed runs and shows, in every one of them, the
prologue completing in **7-13 seconds** and the gate-scratch breadcrumb (line 214, the last
head section) landing normally — then 231 seconds of silence, then the kill. The head sections
run to completion on runs that are killed.

A 25-minute head gap is roughly **four to five missed runs** at the observed 5-6 minute
cadence. Whatever causes it either drops whole runs or fails the head's
`aws cloudwatch put-metric-data` calls. Both are outside `9313`'s mechanism.

This ticket exists so that the head gap is investigated on its own evidence rather than folded
into `9313` on a plausible story — the exact error `9313`'s own investigation had to correct
twice.

## Leads, explicitly UNCONFIRMED

1. **Cadence pressure.** A killed run occupies 240s of a ~300s timer period, leaving ~60s of
   slack, so any additional delay pushes a run past the next elapse. Change 2684 takes a run to
   ~105s, restoring ~195s. **If the head gap narrows after 2684 deploys, this was a
   contributing factor.** If it does not, the defect is independent. Check this FIRST — it is
   free, and it partitions the search.
2. **The `aws` CLI itself.** It is a Python process started fresh for every metric; under the
   memory pressure documented on this host (the mcp container at ~1.7 GB RSS) its startup could
   be slow or it could be killed. A failing `put-metric-data` is invisible today: every call is
   `2>/dev/null || true`.
3. **Timer elapse being skipped.** `OnUnitActiveSec` is measured from the last COMPLETED
   activation; `1205-63b2-2c01-4e7f` already found one latch mode here.

## What makes this diagnosable now

Change 2684 publishes `probe_ok`, `probe_elapsed_seconds` and `probe_truncated`. Before it,
run duration and run completion were visible only in `systemctl` and in no metric at all —
which is why `9313` took a day. Start this investigation from those three, not from the
absence of other metrics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The head gap is reproduced and attributed by measurement — whether a run was started, and
      whether the head's `put-metric-data` calls succeeded — not inferred from metric absence.
- [ ] Lead 1 is settled first: state whether the gap narrows after 2684 deploys, with numbers.
- [ ] If the `aws` calls are failing, their failure becomes observable rather than swallowed by
      `2>/dev/null || true`.
- [ ] The four alarms named above stop firing on absence while their conditions are healthy,
      without their thresholds changing.
- [ ] Portability: host shell + systemd + local validation; no dependence on a single CI provider.

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-05 by an independent CloudWatch presence sweep (period=300, 96 buckets/metric)
run while `9313` was in review. The sweep's headline finding — a monotone decline in metric
presence with script position, 93% at the head down to 43% at the tail and 0% for
`var_tmp_used_percent` — CONFIRMS `9313`. The head number is the residue that `9313` does not
explain, and this ticket is that residue.
data.title: The observability probe's HEAD-of-script metrics gap for up to 25 minutes, which the section-truncation root cause cannot explain — a second, independent publishing defect
